title: sqlparse: split() stops splitting BEGIN TRANSACTION blocks
bug_report: After upgrading sqlparse, sqlparse.split() no longer splits a script wrapped in BEGIN TRANSACTION; ... END TRANSACTION; into separate statements. A script with BEGIN TRANSACTION, a DELETE, an INSERT and END TRANSACTION comes back as a single statement instead of four, which breaks our migration runner.
handwritten_test:
import sqlparse


def test_split_transaction_block():
    sql = 'BEGIN TRANSACTION;\nDELETE FROM a USING b WHERE a.id = b.id;\nINSERT INTO a SELECT * FROM b;\nEND TRANSACTION;'
    assert len(sqlparse.split(sql)) == 4

title: pathspec: the gitignore pattern * stops matching files in subdirectories
bug_report: Since upgrading pathspec, the gitignore pattern '*' no longer matches files inside subdirectories such as 'anydir/file.txt'. A spec meant to match everything except product_dir/ (lines '*' and '!product_dir/') now matches nothing at all, so tools that rely on it (like black's excludes) behave wrongly.
handwritten_test:
import pathspec


def test_star_matches_subdirectories():
    spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines('gitwildmatch', ['*', '!product_dir/'])
    assert spec.match_file('anydir/file.txt') is True
    assert spec.match_file('product_dir/file.txt') is False

title: sql-metadata: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reports the wrong table (dependency bump)
bug_report: Parser("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS foo (bar INT NULL);").tables used to return ['foo']. Now it returns ['IF NOT EXISTS'], so our lineage tool records a table literally called IF NOT EXISTS. Nothing in our code changed.

title: Python-Markdown: backslashes in raw HTML attributes get mangled
bug_report: After upgrading Markdown, an inline raw HTML tag like comes out of markdown.markdown() as src="..\46.oo.png" - backslashes inside HTML attributes get corrupted into numbers.
handwritten_test:
import markdown def test_backslashes_in_raw_html_attribute(): out = markdown.markdown('') assert out == '

'
